body:
#2065's Build (ubuntu-latest) IS RED, AND IT IS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT THE IMPLEMENTER'S DOING - but I could not establish the cause, and I want to be precise about which of those two things I verified.

THE FAILURE: `scaffold_refresh::tests::starter_role_refresh_adds_missing_prompt_and_preserves_user_prompt`, panicking at scaffold_refresh.rs:387 with "legacy role should be refreshed". 5291 passed, 1 failed.

WHY IT LOOKS UNRELATED - this part is solid. #2065's diff touches rel-type parsing (git_backend_cmd.rs, three functions in lib.rs) and two test files. It does not touch scaffold_refresh, roles, or scaffolding. And the branch's merge-base is EXACTLY b54065148a - the BUG-1464 commit that INTRODUCED this test - whose own main CI run was green. So the identical test code passed on main and failed on main-plus-one-unrelated-commit.

TWO THINGS I CHECKED AND RULED OUT, so nobody re-walks them:

1. NOT AN UNLOCKED ENV RACE. The test mutates HOME and AIDA_TEST_HOME, which are process-global, and Rust runs tests in parallel threads - so I went looking for a sibling test mutating them without the lock. glyphs.rs has thirteen direct `set_var("AIDA_TEST_HOME")` calls, which looked exactly like it. It is not: every one is inside a test that calls `lock()`, which delegates to the SAME `crate::test_env::env_lock()` the EnvVarsGuard uses, with a BUG-697 comment saying that is precisely why. The guard's SAFETY precondition holds. I had this written up as a finding and killed it on the last check.

2. NOT A STALE BASE. The branch contains b54065148a; it is missing only a7ef44862c (#1978's merge), which touches forge/drain code and no scaffolding.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, AND A CORRECTION TO MYSELF. I first read `gh run list` as showing BOTH a success and a failure on bug-1471-work at the same sha - which would have been nondeterminism proven outright. That read was wrong: those two rows are the MERGE-HOLD-GATE workflow, green at 22:30 before I placed the hold and red at 22:37 after, which is the gate doing its job. There is exactly ONE CI run on this branch and it failed.

So I have a single observation. I CANNOT CALL IT FLAKY - one red run is not evidence of nondeterminism, it is evidence of one red run. The honest statement is: the failure is in code the PR does not touch, at a base that was green, cause unknown.

THE DECISIVE EXPERIMENT IS A RE-RUN AT THE SAME SHA, and this is the one case where that is the right instrument rather than the usual trap. `gh run rerun` normally proves nothing because it re-tests the same commit - which is exactly what you want when the question is whether the same commit produces the same result. Same sha, same code, different outcome = nondeterministic. Same sha, same failure = real and interaction-driven, and then it matters a great deal, because it would mean an unrelated one-commit delta can turn that test red.

I am not re-running it myself - that is dispatch, and it burns CI on a PR already refused on its own merits. Flagging it as the next step for whoever picks up the rework.

BEARING ON MY VERDICT: none. #2065 stays CHANGES REQUESTED on F1-F3, which are all about the diff itself. The rework will re-run CI anyway, and if it comes back green at a new sha that still tells us nothing about this question - so if anyone wants the answer, the rerun has to happen at bfef2601b1 before the branch moves.
subject: #2065 Build red on a test it does not touch — cause NOT established, two mechanisms ruled out, and I withdraw my own 'both success and failure' read
